QuickCapture.Guide.Title: Start taking notes
QuickCapture.Guide.Body:
# Start with one note

This sample note is yours to edit or delete. Enter text, then switch between **Edit** and **Preview** to see your Markdown.

## What you can do

- Capture ideas, meeting notes, links, and temporary information; a title is optional
- Pin frequently used content to the Pinned tab and unpin it whenever you need to
- With clipboard history enabled, copied text, links, and images appear in the Clipboard tab
- Drag images or files into a note, or add and remove attachments in its details
- Search titles and note text to find an earlier record

## Markdown cheat sheet

| What to write | Example input |
| --- | --- |
| Bold text | `**Important**` |
| Task list | `- [ ] Follow up` |
| Link | `[DeskBox](https://deskbox.fun)` |

```md
## Meeting notes
- [ ] Confirm the next step
- [ ] Attach the reference material
```

> This sample is ordinary content. Once you rewrite it, it stays with your notes.
Todo.Guide.Title: Start with your first task

Todo.Guide.Step.Schedule: Set a date and reminder in the details
Todo.Guide.Step.BreakDown: Add more steps to break the task down
Todo.Guide.Notes:
# Use this task to explore Todo

Check the three steps above one by one. When they are all complete, the task moves to Completed; you can uncheck it to keep working.

## Task details

| Feature | When it helps |
| --- | --- |
| Importance and color | Separate priorities, projects, or contexts |
| Date and reminder | Set a follow-up time for time-sensitive work |
| Recurrence | Handle daily, weekly, or regular tasks |
| Attachments | Keep reference files, images, or materials |

## Write the details in Notes

Put longer context, decisions, and progress here with Markdown. You can also add lists and code-style text:

```text
Meeting outcome
1. Confirm the owner
2. Follow up on Friday
```

- [ ] Add background information
- [ ] Attach reference material

> Delete or rewrite this sample task, then start adding your own.

Settings.Dialog.SupportP1: Thank you for using DeskBox and for caring about its future. The Microsoft Store and direct-download editions offer the same features; they mainly differ in how they are installed and updated.

Settings.Dialog.AboutMeP1: I like the native feel of Microsoft apps, and I like widgets that keep useful information and tools close on the desktop.
Settings.Dialog.AboutMeP2: Microsoft has never made this kind of desktop widget a sustained focus, so I started building DeskBox. I want it to feel at home on Windows while solving practical desktop organization and everyday-use problems.

Onboarding.Intro.Body: Keep files, notes, and tasks together in lightweight desktop widgets

Settings.Search.Everything.About.P1: File and folder search in DeskBox is powered by Everything, a free third-party desktop search engine. DeskBox queries Everything's existing index for instant results and merges them with your DeskBox content — notes, todos, and settings — in the same search popup.
Settings.Search.Everything.About.P3: Everything is developed by voidtools and is not bundled with DeskBox. File search requires Everything to be installed and running; when it is missing, DeskBox shows a reminder instead of failing.

Onboarding.Task.Step1.Title: Your first file widget is on the right
Onboarding.Task.Step1.Body: A file widget is a place to organize files on your desktop. Put frequently used files in it, then show or hide it anytime.

Onboarding.Task.Step2.Body: A collection widget is not a shortcut. Files you drag or paste are moved or copied into the storage path below. Every collection widget creates its own folder under this path.
